SddModule.keywords: module-decomposition, module-map, entity-inventory, dbc-contracts, ports-adapters, closed-world, file-structure, modes, add-module, refine-module, sdd-module
SddModule.Mission:
Turn an approved `product` / `library` scope spec into a hierarchy of module specs: a closed-world entity inventory, an explicit public surface per entity, strict DbC contracts (Ports / Adapters / Services), and a designed file structure. Loaded lazily by the router; inherits the router core (language, dialogue, safeguard, diverge, no-narration, stateless) — not repeated here.
Input — `specs//.spec.md`. Output — `specs///.spec.md` (nesting allowed) + the scope spec Module Map updated (append-only per module). Only for scope-type product / library.
Out of scope: task tickets, BDD, execution plans, rules linkage — those belong to scaffold. The canonical worked example lives in the étalon (referenced at the write step), not inlined here.
**Glossary.** Modes: initial · add-module · refine-module. Port = abstraction introduced ONLY on confirmed variability (≥2 impls) or an explicit test seam; a single impl without that is a Service, not a Port.

BeliefState.deps: AX_OPERATOR_LANGUAGE, AX_OPERATOR_DIALOGUE_STYLE, AX_DIALOGUE_DISCIPLINE, AX_OPERATOR_SAFEGUARD, AX_NO_PROCESS_NARRATION, AX_STATELESS_ARTIFACT, AX_SCALE_PROPORTIONAL_DEPTH
BeliefState.Axiom: Each directive runs in one of several modes, auto-detected from operator intake. Mode controls step branching and which axioms apply. The concrete mode set is directive-specific (e.g. `greenfield` / `refine` / `pivot`; `initial` / `extend-dag`; `initial` / `add-module` / `refine-module`).

Mode detection is mechanical and table-driven from intake (artifact presence + operator verb). Ambiguous intake never defaults silently → HALT and ask the operator (binary disambiguation where possible). The detection table is directive-specific.

Module decomposition applies ONLY to scope-type=product and scope-type=library. - scope-type=infrastructure → `H_INVALID_SCOPE_TYPE` (use discovery for infrastructure scopes; they have their own Effective Rules section). - scope-type=interface → `H_INVALID_SCOPE_TYPE` (interface scopes define interfaces, not modules).

Phase reads specs only, never code; no project-wide search (grep / find / ripgrep) outside the reads explicitly listed by the directive. `audit` is the only directive permitted to read code; it alone resolves spec/code mismatch.

**Every rule activates through an explicit operator decision — never silently.** The decision is two-staged: Stage A locks the relevance shortlist per category with the operator; Stage B walks the axioms of `architecture/*` and `infra/*` rules for Accept (default) / Adapt / Override. Every deviation from a rule default lands in the Decision Log. `coding/*` / `testing/*` rules stay deferred — the phase-subagent loads them at phase entry per `phase-execution-protocol`.

A recommendation must be the result of a search, not the first typical answer. Aligned models collapse to the modal option; a single quick recommendation usually IS that mode, which is rarely the best fit for a specific task.
On any non-trivial or design / architecture question, before recommending: - Internally enumerate a diverse set of candidate options with a rough sense of how typical each is, deliberately reaching past the obvious ones into the tail (verbalized-sampling style). - Judge them against THIS task's constraints, not against generic typicality. - Recommend the option that best fits the task — and when it is a non-obvious (tail) choice, say so and why it beats the obvious one.
Stakes gate the presentation (see `AX_DIALOGUE_DISCIPLINE`): on a high-stakes / architecture question, present the strongest alternatives WITHOUT pre-anchoring a single pick, or pair the recommendation with the strongest alternative and the reason; on low-stakes, a direct recommendation is fine.

Module boundaries are decided by the operator. The agent proposes 2–3 decomposition variants along different axes (by feature, by layer, by data ownership, by lifecycle). No unilateral pick. Final decomposition recorded in scope spec's Decision Log: which axis was chosen and why.

When proposing scope or module candidates, draw the boundary along three axes, never mixed into one unit: data / domain (business rules, state, persistence) ↔ UI / presentation (view, rendering, user interaction) ↔ infrastructure (transport, deployment, third-party wiring). A candidate spanning two axes is a signal to split it, not a shortcut to take. A shared core is extracted from these axes only once ≥2 real consumers need it — never speculatively (`AX_YAGNI_OVERENGINEERING_GUARD`); a single consumer stays inline.

Hierarchy, not flat list. Sub-modules → nested structure: `specs////.spec.md`. Depth unlimited; each level must be justified — nesting for its own sake is forbidden. All specs are cross-linked.
Growth is the decomposition trigger: a module that outgrows its cohesion splits into sub-modules and becomes a thin index over them, as a scope indexes its modules (`AX_SCOPE_STAYS_THIN`). The size limit is held by tooling, not narrative instruction — `sdd-check` flags an over-budget module spec and the `module` flow offers the operator decomposition (split the world) or compression (tighten the spec).
Behavior is the second decomposition trigger, independent of size: an entity OWNING BEHAVIOR — own state, a lifecycle with transitions, error handling, or direct user interaction (input / gesture / keyboard) — earns its own spec even inside a module far under the size budget, which becomes a thin index over it exactly as the size trigger does. A purely presentational leaf — props in, markup out, zero decisions — stays a one-line index row, no spec of its own. Marker: a component holding local state or handling a keypress owns behavior; one that only paints the props it is handed does not.
Held by tooling: `sdd-check` flags a decomposed module missing from its parent's links (`SDD_MODULE_NOT_IN_INDEX`).

The `module` flow owns TWO sections in the scope spec (`specs//.spec.md`):
- **Module Map** (`Module Map`) — append-only rows per module. - **Approved Usage Example** (`Usage Example` section — library / product) — composition view. Every `module` flow session (`initial` / `add-module` / `refine-module`) rewrites this section as one user-facing flow over the current module set. Module-level snippets NOT inlined — anchor-link to each module's `Module Usage Example`. Skip rewrite only when scope has zero modules with public surface.
**Bidirectional consistency check** before session close — both directions must pass: - (→) every named abstraction in scope-spec Usage Example has a home in some module's `Entity Inventory`; - (←) every module with public surface (≥1 entry in `Entity Surfaces`) either appears in scope-spec Usage Example OR carries `internal-only — not in composition view` in its `Module Decision Log`.
Failure of either direction → fix the gap before STEP_6 finishes; do NOT close session with inconsistency.
All other scope-spec sections (Vision, Requirements & Constraints, Architecture, Decision Log, Handoff) remain untouched. Cross-scope module dependencies → `Scope Reference` in module-spec `Inter-Module Dependencies`, never a direct reference to another product scope's modules.
The `module` flow does NOT write to `specs/README.md` (that is the `root` flow's sole property).

A scope spec has a bounded role: Vision, Requirements, Architecture decisions, Decision Log, Module Map, composition Usage Example, Handoff, Bootstrap Requirements. Entity inventory, public surfaces, DbC contracts, and file layout are module-level — they live ONLY in module specs (`AX_HIERARCHICAL_SPECS`), never inline in the scope spec.
Two representations: - **monolithic** — no modules yet; the scope spec may hold design inline (early / small scope). - **index** — once decomposed, the scope spec is a thin composition over its modules: Module Map + Usage Example linking to each module's usage example; the detail lives in the modules.
Growth is the decomposition signal, not a license to expand. When scope-level design reaches entity / contract / file granularity, that detail moves into a module — it does NOT accumulate in the scope spec. A scope converges to a thin index; it does not grow without bound.
First decomposition is a migration: the `initial` module session moves entity-level detail out of the scope spec into the new module specs, leaving the scope spec in the index representation. The same rule recurses — a module that reaches sub-module granularity sheds detail into sub-modules and stays an index over them.
Held by tooling: `sdd-check` flags a bloated scope index (`SDD_SCOPE_BLOATED`) and, recursing the same rule to a module with child modules beneath it, a parent module that has not become a thin index (`SDD_PARENT_MODULE_NOT_INDEX`).

In `refine-module` mode existing public surface is preserved unless explicitly retired with operator approval.
Refinement = adding entities, tightening contracts (preconditions can become stricter, postconditions cannot become weaker), or fixing wrong details. Removing a public entity or weakening postconditions is a breaking change requiring a Decision Log entry with operator-confirmed `Risk accepted`.
A breaking change additionally emits a Pivot Invalidation List (`PIVOT_INVALIDATION_LIST_FORMAT`) in this module's spec: its consumer modules — the siblings whose `Inter-Module Dependencies` declares an edge `--> this-module` — listed as `refine-module` targets, plus their tasks to reopen. Consumers are derived from the reverse edges of the module graph; audit verifies every listed item is addressed via `AX_STALE_AFTER_PIVOT_VERIFICATION`. Symmetric to a scope `pivot` — a breaking module change does not close while a consumer is left silently stale.
Refinement preserves the Entity Inventory closed-world commitment: post-refinement inventory is still complete. New entities go into the inventory in the same session.
Module spec body is reworked in place where needed; full predecessor state lives in git history.

A spec lives in two states. **master** — clean file (no Change Manifest, no marks), the target on the main branch. **review-state** — the same file on a working branch during a change: the target text is written IN PLACE (everything else byte-for-byte, so the branch diff reads like a normal PR), with a temporary `CHANGE_MANIFEST` (`CHANGE_MANIFEST_FORMAT`) at the top and affected lines marked `✚` (new) / `~` (changed). New IDs are appended to the end of their section; existing IDs are never renumbered.
`greenfield` (∅ → review-state): the first version is written directly as review-state with `ТИП: greenfield` and NO per-line marks (everything is new — the diff against an empty file already shows it). `refine` / `pivot` edit an existing master in place WITH marks.
The spec change is a reviewable PR (design-PR): the internal critic loop runs first (necessary but NOT sufficient), then the diff goes to EXTERNAL review and the session waits. **compress** (review-state → master) fires ONLY when external review approves — the operator says «no comments» — NOT on internal-critic CLEAN and NOT on a timer. On approval: remove the `CHANGE_MANIFEST` whole, strip the `✚`/`~` marks (lines stay), resolve any ID collisions in one commit, and for `pivot` mark superseded decisions; then merge. Implementation (scaffold → execute) follows the merged master — the design is approved before it is built.
A spec MUST NOT be left in review-state once its change is closed — that is drift the tools track (`sdd-check`): a malformed review-state or a manifest lingering past its lifetime is surfaced with the reason, so the agent fixes it or escalates.

Entity inventory is a closed world. For every module the agent lists ALL entities explicitly. Phrases like «и т.д.», «etc.», «and similar» are forbidden. Before approval, the agent makes the explicit drift-commitment captured in `ENTITY_INVENTORY_FORMAT`.

Entity surface is exhaustive per `ENTITY_SURFACE_FORMAT`: Type, Public Properties, Public Operations (intent-level, no language signatures), Lifecycle, Events, Errors & Degradation, Consumers. No private detail — that is Executor's job.

The diagram floor is a fixed ladder by decomposition stage, not one "when useful" Overview picture — the same discipline agent-inbox's `AX_COMPREHENSION_LADDER` applies to a review applies here to a design, at authoring time instead of review time. Four rungs, each answering ONE distinct question — no two rungs answer the same thing; the worked example lives in `ai/directives/sdd-v2/formats/module-diagram-ladder.example.md`: 1. **Overview** (module spec) — WHAT this module does, main happy-path flow. Unconditional. Held by tooling: `sdd-check` fails a missing section (`SDD_NO_DIAGRAM_BLOCK`) or an empty one (`SDD_DIAGRAM_BLOCK_EMPTY`). The `Inter-Module Dependencies` graph is machine-parsed and does NOT satisfy this rung. 2. **Module Map** (scope spec, `STEP_1_MODULE_MAP`) — WHERE each module sits along the decomposition axes (data/domain ↔ UI ↔ infrastructure, `AX_SEPARATION_OF_CONCERNS`). Unconditional whenever ≥2 modules exist. 3. **Entity Inventory** (`STEP_2_ENTITY_INVENTORY`) — HOW entities relate (ER sketch). Conditional: ≥2 entities in one module connected by reference/ownership/composition. A single entity, or a set with no real relation, states that explicitly and skips it. 4. **Entity Surface** (`STEP_3_ENTITY_SURFACE`) — the entity's LIFECYCLE, when it is a real state machine (≥3 distinct states/transitions, not just create→terminate). Conditional, per entity. 5. **Module Contracts** (`STEP_4_CONTRACTS_DBC`) — the dependency GRAPH among Ports / Adapters / Services. Mandatory whenever the module has ≥1 Port or Adapter; a Service-only module states so explicitly instead of a silently missing graph — floor, never nothing. Each rung is drawn as ASCII in chat at the step that owns it, BEFORE that step's Approval Check — a diagram appearing for the first time in the written spec means the operator never saw the shape they are approving (`AX_CHAT_BEFORE_SPEC`); an Approval Check without it is the same class of violation as `H_ASK_BEFORE_FORMAT` (asked before shown), and the operator may reject and demand it. Beyond these five rungs, the author adds more views (sequence, data-flow, before/after) wherever a further diagram genuinely helps a reader — that part stays judgment, never a gate.

A module spec reads top-down: a human-readable summary on top, heavy contract detail folded beneath. Entity Surfaces and Module Contracts wrap their body in `…` so a reader sees the shape without wading through every precondition. Held by tooling: `sdd-check` fails an unfolded heavy section (`SDD_SECTION_NOT_FOLDED`). This is the spec-artifact analogue of the chat-output `AX_PROGRESSIVE_DISCLOSURE` — summary first, detail on demand.

No consumer — no component (YAGNI). Every entity has explicit `Consumers`: - Internal: future file path or another inventory entity name. - External: textual description (CLI, External API, Browser, OS Event Bus, …).
Consumer is «future feature» without v1-scope confirmation → entity removed or marked `deferred`.

- Business logic depends on Ports, not Adapters, when a Port exists. Port is preferred: preconditions / postconditions / invariants live on the Port, and the Adapter references it and describes side effects + runtime backing + verification levels. When the module consciously forgoes a Port (single implementation, no confirmed variability or test seam), the same DbC contract lives directly on the Service / Adapter instead — the absence of a Port is not the absence of a contract; that choice is recorded in the Decision Log (`AX_DECISION_LOG_REQUIRED`). - Port introduced only with confirmed v1 variability (≥2 implementations) or explicit test seam. Single implementation without confirmed split → Service or Entity, not Port. - Every proposed abstraction requires justification: which current risk / constraint / consumer it closes. - **Contract obligation follows BEHAVIOR, not entity type.** Any entity that owns behavior — its own state, a lifecycle, error handling, or direct user interaction — carries a DbC contract (Pre / Post / On-violation per operation, plus loading/empty/error states where they apply), a UI component included; "component" is not a free pass. Only a purely-rendering entity (props in, markup out, zero decisions) is exempt, and the exemption must be an explicit `Presentation-Only` marker on that entity's Entity Surface (`ENTITY_SURFACE_FORMAT`) — an entity with neither a contract nor that marker is a spec omission, not a legitimate style choice. - **DbC section shape is flexible.** `Module Contracts (DbC)` carries any subset of subsections drawn from the entity Type vocabulary (Port, Adapter, Service, Component, Pattern, Utility, Module-level invariants, …). Ports/Adapters are AVAILABLE, not mandatory: single-implementation modules legitimately use Service-only, Component-only, or Pattern-only DbC. Subsections are unnumbered `###` headers (e.g. `### Ports`, `### Components`, `### OperationDef Pattern`).

DbC is derived from context, not only from DX code. Scope spec Requirements & Constraints is mandatory source for preconditions, invariants, fallback semantics, trust boundaries. A contract cannot be reduced to «what to do» while ignoring «under what conditions it must not».

DbC contracts are textual and language-agnostic. Write preconditions / postconditions / invariants and public operations as plain intent-level statements in the shared vocabulary (Port, Adapter, Entity, Command, Query, Event) — one testable statement per line, readable, free of syntax noise. Concrete signatures and types belong to the execution phase: the coding rules turn the contract into the project's language there. The single exception: the Usage Example / usage examples are written in the project's target language — they show consumption, the contract stays textual. A genuinely cross-language contract belongs in an `interface` scope, expressed in its own interface language (schema / proto / IDL), not here.

Runtime backing and verification levels in every contract that depends on platform/runtime hooks. Two orthogonal axes: - `Runtime Backing` (single value): `not-implemented` | `simulation` | `real-runtime`. What's actually behind the public surface in production code. - `Verification Levels` (multi-value): subset of `contract` | `unit` | `integration` | `e2e`. - `Deferred Runtime Scope` (if part of declared behavior is not yet backed by real runtime).
Simulation must not be declared as runtime: marking `real-runtime` while the implementation is simulation-only, without an explicit `Deferred Runtime Scope`, is forbidden.

Public options cannot be silently forgotten. All include flags, transport settings, platform-specific options mentioned in scope spec must either bind to a concrete Port/Adapter contract or be explicitly marked `deferred / not consumed in v1` with a pointer to the task or version that activates them.
Single namespace for grepability. Module-wide: `` / ``. Files: `-*.`. Types/classes/constants: `*`. Platform-specific: `--*.`, `*`. Goal: `rg ` or `rg -` finds all related code.
No God Objects. File size ≤1500 lines. File structure (phase `FILE_STRUCTURE`) physically separates `ports/` (or `contracts/`) from `adapters/` (or `impl/`).
YAGNI. Every module, entity, Port has explicit v1 consumer or near-term variability. Future-proofing without a confirmed consumer is forbidden.

The directive runs on an explicit frame stack with a defined main path of phases. Disputes / dives / sub-topics open a nested frame; the stack is visible in the trace header. A sub-topic never silently stalls the parent frame. The concrete main path is directive-specific.

Every non-obvious decision → a Decision Log entry in `DECISION_LOG_ENTRY_FORMAT` — one line, the expanded part in parentheses: `D-NNN — (почему: …; отвергнуто: …; риск: …)`; IDs are stable. Non-obvious only (`AX_DECISION_LOG_NON_OBVIOUS`): a pick already recorded in the spec's own tables is never duplicated as a DL row. Which decisions qualify and which Decision Log receives the entry are specified per directive.

Separate Facts / Assumptions / Hypotheses in every intake-style frame. - **Facts** — directly observable from input artifacts (spec, sibling specs, rule files, extracted measurements). - **Assumptions** — working assumptions awaiting confirmation; mark explicitly. - **Hypotheses** — conjectures that require operator validation before they are promoted to requirements.
Conflating the three causes downstream decisions to be made on unvalidated assumptions, producing requirements mismatches that surface only at integration; surface them in distinct lists.

External research (WebSearch/WebFetch) run in this session ALWAYS lands as a research document via `npx gennady sdd-new research --scope --slug ` — filled in BEFORE the result feeds a proposal to the operator; a chat summary is not storage (session dies, research dies with it). Every factual claim must be re-verifiable: traced to a source (a specific page, URL + access date; for code-derived facts — path + commit) OR explicitly flagged `agent conclusion` / `from model memory as of `. A fact carrying neither is a document defect, not a style choice. A repeat question checks existing `specs/**/research/` first — supersede, never duplicate.

Final hierarchy contains: - per-module spec Handoff: implementation/test files Scaffolder will create; explicit stack dependencies (language, test framework) Scaffolder resolves against `ai/directives/coding/*`, `ai/directives/testing/*`; **Module Rules Additions** layered on scope-wide baseline. - Modules layer rules ADD-only (cannot remove scope-wide). Categories: `coding` | `testing` | `architecture` | `quality`. No additions → block is explicitly `None`, not omitted. Cascade union (traversed-scopes ∪ target-scope ∪ module ∪ task) is computed by Scaffolder per-task.

Before writing any operator-facing artifact, recall the language rules — `AX_OPERATOR_DIALOGUE_STYLE` (bureaucratic noun-for-verb phrasing, literal calque, bookish word) and `AX_READER_WITHOUT_SESSION_CONTEXT` (a branch name, «как обсуждали», a session-plan label) — and hold the text about to be written to them. This is the author's own pass, done in the moment of writing, not a report to the operator. The independent post-check (lint, audit) stays separate and unchanged — this pass does not replace it.

A mutation is not done until its scope passes the mechanical check. Any flow that creates or evolves an artifact under a scope — spec, module, ticket, DAG, tracker — closes by running `sdd-check` on the affected scope (`sdd-check --all specs/`; portal, task-DAG, tracker, or cross-scope work → `sdd-check --all .`) and resolving or consciously deferring every finding before handing off.

SddModule.HaltConditions: | 🛑 ID | Trigger | |---|---| | `H_INVALID_SCOPE_TYPE` | scope-type = infrastructure or interface — module-decomposition not applicable | | `H_SCOPE_SPEC_MISSING` | `specs//.spec.md` does not exist — run the scope flow first | | `H_INCOMPLETE_SCOPE_SPEC` | Scope spec missing required sections (Vision, Architecture, Golden DX) | | `H_AMBIGUOUS_MODE` | Module specs exist + mode verb absent + no Pivot Invalidation List | | `H_LOW_CONFIDENCE` | Confidence LOW at decomposition lock or final hierarchy | | `H_INVENTORY_NOT_APPROVED` | Entered the surface step without all-module inventories approved | | `H_REFINE_BREAKING_CHANGE_NO_LOG` | `refine-module` removes a public entity / weakens a postcondition without a Decision Log entry (`AX_DECISION_LOG_REQUIRED`) | | `H_REFINE_BREAKING_NO_IMPACT_LIST` | breaking `refine-module` without a Pivot Invalidation List enumerating consumer modules (`AX_REFINE_MODULE_PRESERVES_CONTRACTS`) | | `H_MISSING_RULE_FILE` | A module rule reference does not resolve to an existing file (and not `deferred`) | | `H_OPERATOR_REJECT` | Operator refused decomposition, inventory, surface, contract, structure, or final hierarchy | | `H_ASK_BEFORE_FORMAT` | A step's Approval Check fires before the step's own format contract (`READ_AND_USE_DIRECTIVE`) was read this turn — operator may reject and demand the step redone read-first |

Step.Action: Read `specs//.spec.md` (sole source per `AX_SPEC_IS_SOLE_SOURCE`). Missing → `H_SCOPE_SPEC_MISSING`; incomplete → `H_INCOMPLETE_SCOPE_SPEC`. scope-type must be product / library (`AX_SCOPE_TYPE_GATE`, else `H_INVALID_SCOPE_TYPE`). Mode per `AX_MODE_AUTO_DETECT_OR_HALT` — initial / add-module / refine-module; the mode picked here controls step branching downstream (`AX_DIRECTIVE_MODE`). On `add-module` / `refine-module`, run `sdd-check --all specs/` first — an over-budget module (`SDD_MODULE_OVERSIZED` → decompose, `SDD_MODULE_SPEC_VERBOSE` → compress) is surfaced to the operator BEFORE new work, per `AX_HIERARCHICAL_SPECS`.

Step.Goal: Lock module boundaries; update the scope Module Map.
Step.Action: `READ_AND_USE_DIRECTIVE("ai/directives/sdd-v2/formats/module-map-update.xml")` first — this step's Approval Check asked before that read is `H_ASK_BEFORE_FORMAT`. Module decomposition does not require external research by default (`AX_SCALE_PROPORTIONAL_DEPTH` — that gate lives in the scope flow's Architecture step); but if a decomposition pattern or approach proposed below WAS informed by a WebSearch / WebFetch pass this session, persist it per `AX_RESEARCH_PERSISTED` — `npx gennady sdd-new research --scope --slug `, filled — BEFORE presenting the boundaries, and link the document in this message; research performed and left only in chat is the violation, not the research itself. Propose module boundaries along `AX_SEPARATION_OF_CONCERNS` (data/domain ↔ UI/presentation ↔ infrastructure; a shared core only once ≥2 consumers need it) — draw the decomposition as a diagram, not a bullet list of names: one tier per axis (data/domain · UI/presentation · infrastructure), each candidate module placed under its axis, as an ASCII block in THIS message (rung 2 of `AX_SPEC_MANDATORY_DIAGRAM`; worked shape in `ai/directives/sdd-v2/formats/module-diagram-ladder.example.md`) — this diagram IS what the operator confirms next, not a restatement of it. The operator confirms (`AX_MODULE_BOUNDARY_BY_OPERATOR`). **Diagram shown, this message, before the Approval Check below** — its absence is the same class of violation as `H_ASK_BEFORE_FORMAT` (asked before shown); the operator may reject and demand it. Update the scope spec Module Map append-only (`AX_SCOPE_SPEC_MODULE_MAP_OWNERSHIP`), converting the same shape to the mermaid `flowchart` grouped by axis (`AX_CHAT_BEFORE_SPEC`) — never a diagram invented fresh at write time. `add-module` appends only (`AX_APPEND_ONLY_MODULE_ADD`). On `initial` this is the monolith→index migration (`AX_SCOPE_STAYS_THIN`): move entity / contract / file-level detail out of the scope spec into the new module specs, leaving the scope spec as the thin index (Module Map + composition Golden DX). Apply BOTH decomposition triggers while drawing any boundary here — size (`AX_HIERARCHICAL_SPECS` budget, held by `sdd-check`) and behavior (an entity owning state, a lifecycle, error handling, or user interaction) — and name explicitly, in this message, which entities earn their own child spec and which stay a one-line index row. The two rules are one seen from two steps: an entity that earns a spec here for owning behavior carries the full per-operation DbC contract there (`AX_PORTS_AND_ABSTRACTIONS_DISCIPLINE`, `STEP_4_CONTRACTS_DBC`) — the index itself holds only links to child specs plus one row per presentation-only leaf, never an inlined contract. Approval Check. STOP.

`READ_AND_USE_DIRECTIVE("ai/directives/sdd-v2/formats/entity-inventory-format.xml")` first — the Approval Check below asked before that read is `H_ASK_BEFORE_FORMAT`. List every entity of the module — the complete world (`AX_CLOSED_WORLD_INVENTORY`); anything an execution agent adds beyond it is drift. Interview the operator via `READ_AND_USE_DIRECTIVE("ai/directives/sdd-v2/interview-protocol.directive.xml")`, extending its coverage map with the decomposition topics: «Пропущенная сущность» (what the inventory still misses) and «Бесхозная ответственность» (a responsibility no listed entity owns). A dispute or tangent raised mid-interview opens a nested frame on the flow's stack — this step's main path never silently stalls on it (`AX_STACK_BASED_FLOW`). Size the interview to the confirmed `scale:` from the session file (`AX_SCALE_PROPORTIONAL_DEPTH`). Keep evidence separated per `AX_EVIDENCE_HYGIENE`: entities named by the scope spec are facts; entities inferred during the interview stay hypotheses until the operator confirms them. Errors are first-class inventory, not an afterthought: either one listed entity is the explicit errors owner, or the inventory carries a module-level `Ошибки: <механизм> → <владелец>` line (mechanism = throw / Result / event / …). A downstream BDD ticket cannot require behavior on an error whose owner is absent from this inventory — surface the gap here, before approval, not at scaffold time. Once ≥2 entities are relationally connected (one references, owns, or is composed of another), draw the ER sketch per `ENTITY_INVENTORY_FORMAT` as an ASCII block in THIS message BEFORE the Approval Check (rung 3 of `AX_SPEC_MANDATORY_DIAGRAM`; worked shape in `ai/directives/sdd-v2/formats/module-diagram-ladder.example.md`) — a single entity or a set with no real relation states that explicitly instead. **Diagram shown (or explicit skip-reason), this message, before Approval Check** — its absence on a ≥2-related-entity inventory is the same class of violation as `H_ASK_BEFORE_FORMAT`. If a module's inventory outgrows cohesion (too many entities / unrelated responsibility clusters), PROPOSE sub-module decomposition here per `AX_HIERARCHICAL_SPECS` — the split is a result of weighing real alternatives, not the first typical cut (`AX_DIVERGE_BEFORE_RECOMMEND`); the operator decides — do not silently let one module absorb a sub-system. All module inventories must be approved before the surface step (else `H_INVENTORY_NOT_APPROVED`). Approval Check. STOP.

`READ_AND_USE_DIRECTIVE("ai/directives/sdd-v2/formats/entity-surface-format.xml")` first — the Approval Check below asked before that read is `H_ASK_BEFORE_FORMAT`. Define each entity's public surface (`AX_ENTITY_SURFACE_COMPLETENESS`), including its `Errors & Degradation` field: which errors, by what mechanism (throw / Result / event / …), and who owns handling/display — do not leave it generic once the inventory named an owner. No consumer → no entity (`AX_CONSUMER_DRIVEN`): an entity without a confirmed v1 consumer is dropped or `deferred`. Show each entity as its own compact block in chat (type / operations / errors) BEFORE asking for confirmation — a batched approval across several entities in one multiSelect/confirmation is fine, but only after every entity in that batch was shown individually, never as a table skim. When an entity's Lifecycle is a real state machine (≥3 distinct states/transitions, not just create→terminate), draw it as an ASCII state diagram per `ENTITY_SURFACE_FORMAT` inside that entity's block, BEFORE the confirmation for that entity (rung 4 of `AX_SPEC_MANDATORY_DIAGRAM`; worked shape in `ai/directives/sdd-v2/formats/module-diagram-ladder.example.md`) — a 2-state lifecycle stays the one-line bullet. **Diagram shown (or below-threshold, stated), this message, before that entity's confirmation** — its absence on a ≥3-transition lifecycle is the same class of violation as `H_ASK_BEFORE_FORMAT`. This step's Approval Check is its own — merging it with STEP_4's or STEP_5's Ask into one combined question is a violation, not an efficiency gain. STOP.

`READ_AND_USE_DIRECTIVE("ai/directives/sdd-v2/formats/dbc-contracts.xml")` first — the Approval Check below asked before that read is `H_ASK_BEFORE_FORMAT`. Preconditions / postconditions per OPERATION — each operation gets its own pre/post lines, plus a mandatory line for what happens when the precondition is violated (e.g. a non-existent id): observable error behavior, not silence. A general block at entity/service level is for genuine class-level invariants only (what stays true across the whole lifetime, independent of any single operation) — do not use it as a substitute for per-operation contracts. Written textual and language-agnostic per `AX_CONTRACTS_TEXTUAL_AGNOSTIC` (target-language code appears only in usage examples). A Port is introduced ONLY on confirmed variability or a test seam (`AX_PORTS_AND_ABSTRACTIONS_DISCIPLINE`) — Port-vs-Service is a design choice, so apply `AX_DIVERGE_BEFORE_RECOMMEND` (do not default to Port); when the module consciously forgoes a Port, the same per-operation DbC lives directly on the Service / Adapter and that choice is recorded in the Decision Log (`AX_DECISION_LOG_REQUIRED`, `DECISION_LOG_ENTRY_FORMAT`). This is entity-type-agnostic (`AX_PORTS_AND_ABSTRACTIONS_DISCIPLINE`) — a Component that owns state, a lifecycle, error handling, or user interaction gets a `### Components` DbC subsection in the same per-operation shape; only an entity explicitly marked `Presentation-Only` on its Entity Surface skips this block. Each abstraction carries its justification (`AX_CONTEXT_TO_CONTRACT`); runtime backing is stated per contract (`AX_RUNTIME_BACKING_IN_CONTRACTS`). Draw the Port/Adapter/Service dependency graph per `DBC_DEPENDENCY_GRAPH_FORMAT` as an ASCII block in THIS message BEFORE the Approval Check (rung 5 of `AX_SPEC_MANDATORY_DIAGRAM`; worked shape in `ai/directives/sdd-v2/formats/module-diagram-ladder.example.md`): nodes = every Port / Adapter / Service this module defines, edges = `implements` (Adapter → Port) and `depends on` (Service → Port), arrows toward the more stable side. A Service-only module (no Port/Adapter at all) states that explicitly instead of a silently missing graph — floor, never nothing. **Diagram shown (or explicit Service-only statement), this message, before the Approval Check below** — its absence is the same class of violation as `H_ASK_BEFORE_FORMAT`. Close the step with two checks before presenting: 1. Every module / entity / Port in the contracts carries a confirmed v1 consumer or near-term variability (`AX_YAGNI_OVERENGINEERING_GUARD`). 2. Every public option / flag / policy the scope spec mentions is bound to a concrete Port / Adapter contract or explicitly marked `deferred / not consumed in v1` with a pointer to the task or version that activates it (`AX_NO_SILENT_OPTION_DROP`). 3. Every entity from `STEP_2_ENTITY_INVENTORY` resolves one of two ways here: a DbC subsection above, or an explicit `Presentation-Only` marker on its Entity Surface (`AX_PORTS_AND_ABSTRACTIONS_DISCIPLINE`) — neither present is a spec omission, surfaced now, not a silently accepted style choice. This step's Approval Check is its own — merging it with STEP_3's or STEP_5's Ask into one combined question is a violation, not an efficiency gain. STOP.

Repo layout; physically split `ports/` (or `contracts/`) from `adapters/` (or `impl/`). No God objects, file size ≤ 1500 lines (`AX_MODULARITY_LIMITS`); single grep namespace (`AX_NAMESPACE_NAMING`). This step's Approval Check is its own — merging it with STEP_3's or STEP_4's Ask into one combined question is a violation, not an efficiency gain. STOP.

On `initial` / `add-module`, for each new module create its skeleton via `sdd-new module --scope --module ` — it never overwrites and prints the section manifest (which sections are REQUIRED and what to fill); on `refine-module` the file already exists, edit it in place, skip `sdd-new`. Content guidance per `READ_AND_USE_DIRECTIVE("ai/directives/sdd-v2/formats/module-spec-structure.xml")` — read it before assembling the spec; an Approval Check on the assembled hierarchy asked before that read is `H_ASK_BEFORE_FORMAT`. Every mermaid diagram this spec carries must already have been shown to the operator as ASCII in chat at the step where that shape was decided, per `AX_CHAT_BEFORE_SPEC` — `READ_AND_USE_DIRECTIVE("ai/directives/sdd-v2/formats/diagram-vocabulary.xml")`; a diagram appearing here for the first time means the operator never saw the shape they are being asked to approve. Assemble each `specs///.spec.md` to it; link back to `../../.spec.md`; reconcile the scope Module Map. In `pivot` / breaking `refine-module` also `READ_AND_USE_DIRECTIVE("ai/directives/sdd-v2/formats/pivot-formats.xml")` (`AX_REFINE_MODULE_PRESERVES_CONTRACTS`, else `H_REFINE_BREAKING_CHANGE_NO_LOG`). For a breaking `refine-module`, derive consumer modules from the reverse edges of the module graph (siblings whose `Inter-Module Dependencies` declares `--> this-module`) and emit a Pivot Invalidation List in the module spec — else `H_REFINE_BREAKING_NO_IMPACT_LIST`. When a module needs rules beyond the scope-wide baseline, fill Module Rules Additions in the Handoff section per `AX_RULE_ACTIVATION` (shortlist + considered-skips, operator locks the list; architecture / infra rules get the per-axiom walk-through); every referenced rule file must resolve, else `H_MISSING_RULE_FILE`. Before writing, run the self-check pass per `AX_ARTIFACT_STYLE_SELF_CHECK`. Write in review-state per `AX_SPEC_LIFECYCLE` — prepend a `CHANGE_MANIFEST` (`READ_AND_USE_DIRECTIVE("ai/directives/sdd-v2/formats/change-manifest.xml")`) and mark changed lines `✚`/`~` (greenfield → manifest only, no per-line marks); compress folds it to master downstream after the change ships. Then run `sdd-check --all specs/` (anchor balance + required sections + links + size budget: `SDD_MODULE_OVERSIZED` / `SDD_MODULE_SPEC_VERBOSE`) and resolve or consciously defer any finding per `AX_CLOSE_WITH_INTEGRITY_CHECK`. Then `READ_AND_USE_DIRECTIVE("ai/directives/sdd-v2/review-lifecycle.directive.xml")` — internal critic → publish (MR) → external review → compress + merge on approval. Only after the spec merges to master, hand off to scaffold (`AX_HANDOFF_TO_TASK_SCAFFOLDING`). Approval Check. STOP.

ChatProtocol.Contract:
Explain, then ask through the tool — a question never fires as bare free-form text. A `### 💡 <О чём решаем>` section header names the decision in plain words (no `Q` numbering, no semantic question IDs); under it, ordinary language explains the question BEFORE any tool call fires — the context, the real options, and a recommendation gated by `AX_DIVERGE_BEFORE_RECOMMEND` (low-stakes: a direct pick is fine; high-stakes / architecture: do not pre-anchor one option — lay out the strongest candidates, a tail one included, or pair the recommendation with its strongest rival and the reason it might win instead). Only once the explanation stands does `AskUserQuestion` fire; its option list mirrors the printed order, short labels only — the argument itself lives in the message, never moved into the tool call.
Batching rule: one `AskUserQuestion` call may carry several questions ONLY when they are mutually independent — answering one does not change the meaning or the options of another (several facets of one single complex decision qualify as one batched call). Dependent questions, and any interview sequence, go one call at a time: compose the next question only after the previous answer is in.
Channel: use `AskUserQuestion` whenever the tool is available. When it is not, fall back to plain text carrying the same shape — the explanation, then an explicit list of named options the operator can answer by name — never restore `Q` labels or per-question IDs; that bare-numbered shape without the tool is itself the violation this contract forbids (`H_UNFORMATTED_ASK`).
Low-stakes — a recommendation is allowed, but only as the result of `AX_DIVERGE_BEFORE_RECOMMEND` (not the first typical answer):
### 💡 Формат хранения токенов Нужно решить, где держать design-токены: сгенерированный JSON проще парсить скриптам, а TS-модуль даёт автокомплит в IDE — для одного пакета без внешних потребителей разница небольшая. ✅ **JSON-файл** `[tokens.json]` — проще парсить любым языком, ничего специфичного для TS. Иначе: - **TS-модуль** `[tokens.ts]` — _за: автокомплит и типы · против: непортируемо за пределы TS_
(AskUserQuestion: «JSON-файл (рекомендую)» · «TS-модуль»)
High-stakes / architecture — do NOT pre-anchor one pick. List the strongest candidates (include a non-obvious / tail one) with «за / против» and let the operator choose; or give a recommendation only alongside its strongest alternative and the reason it might win:
### 💡 Стратегия миграции v1→v2 Три пути дают разный профиль риска и времени простоя, и откат стоит по-разному в каждом. - **Big-bang** `[migrate-all]` — _за: один переход, нет промежуточного состояния · против: долгий простой, откат дорогой_ - **Постепенная миграция по скоупам** `[migrate-incremental]` — _за: откат дешёвый, риск размазан во времени · против: два формата сосуществуют дольше_ - **Parallel-run с shadow-чтением** `[migrate-shadow]` — нетипичный вариант, но снимает риск отката почти полностью ценой временной инфраструктуры
(AskUserQuestion: «Big-bang» · «Постепенная миграция» · «Parallel-run (нетипичный)»)
A plain binary question needs no list — recommendation + inline alternative, still explained before the call:
### 💡 Нужен ли отдельный interface-скоуп Все текущие потребители — web; про API и будущих клиентов явно не говорили. ✅ **Пока не выделять** — можно добавить позже без миграции. _или сразу выделить, если API уже в планах?_
(AskUserQuestion: «Пока не выделять (рекомендую)» · «Выделить сразу»)
A counter-question in reply to a gate is a side-dive, not a rejection: (a) answer the counter-question in full, on its own merits, before returning to the gate; (b) bring the gate back exactly once, marked as a repeat pass, enriched with whatever the counter-question surfaced — «повторяю вопрос» plus a fact or option the side-dive added (e.g. operator asked "как ты делаешь ресёрч?" → the repeat pass adds an option «сначала ресёрч, потом решаем»); a verbatim repeat of the first gate carries no delta and is itself the violation. (c) if the operator answers the repeat pass with another counter-question instead of a pick, do not fire a third pass — stop and ask directly what is blocking the decision.

SddModule.ChatOutput:
Service line — dim, internal, never narrated (per `AX_NO_PROCESS_NARRATION`): `🧩 DM_R · · · conf=`. Breadcrumb milestones (per `BREADCRUMB_FORMAT`): Module Map · Inventory · Surface · Contracts · Files · Hierarchy. Disputes and side-topics open a nested frame on the flow's stack per `AX_STACK_BASED_FLOW` (rendered per `SIDE_DIVE_FORMAT`); the main path never silently stalls.
A step-boundary / decision message (the decision card) is sectioned with markdown headers, in this order. Skip any section empty for this step. During free dialogue inside a step the agent does NOT print this layout — it just talks.
`` — internal anchor + scope + mode + confidence (supplied by the branch)
`` — per `BREADCRUMB_FORMAT`, its OWN paragraph (a blank line above it, not just a `\n`) — markdown collapses a single newline into a space, so without the blank line the breadcrumb visually fuses onto the service line
## `` `` — одной фразой, что делаем
### 🤔 Как я понял задачу — per `UNDERSTANDING_BLOCK_FORMAT` (goes at the TOP) ### 🎯 Главное решение — the crux in plain words; add a diagram per `FLOW_DIAGRAM_WHEN` if it is a flow ### 💡 <О чём решаем> — per `QUESTION_FORMAT` ### ↓ Детали — по желанию — reasoning, full comparison, change-list (per `AX_PROGRESSIVE_DISCLOSURE`)
Glyph dictionary — closed inventory, one assigned meaning each, never a free pick. Every glyph here is chosen to read clearly on BOTH a light and a dark terminal/chat theme — half-tone shading characters (`░ ▒ ▓` and similar) are forbidden anywhere in this layout: they render as near-invisible or vanish outright depending on theme.
Section-header glyphs (fixed, one per header, in the order above): - `🤔` — the agent's own understanding check, at the top of a decision card - `🎯` — the crux decision, in plain words - `💡` — a decision the agent is proposing for the operator to confirm or pick between - `↓` — folded detail, expand on demand
Step-TYPE glyphs (fixed, keyed by the step's TYPE, used in the service line / breadcrumb, never a free pick): - `🏗` — creation / scaffold (new spec, new tickets, new files) - `🔍` — audit / review (fresh-eyes read, no write) - `🔧` — fix / reconcile (spec ⟷ code drift repair) - `⚡` — execute (a task ticket's phases running) - `🗺` — routing / overview (intent classification, project-level map)
Breadcrumb-status glyphs (per `BREADCRUMB_FORMAT`): `✅` done · `👷` active · `◻️` not yet.
No other emoji appear in message or section headers — the glyphs enumerated above are the only ones this layout permits.
One line, its own paragraph below the service line — a blank line separates the two (per `MESSAGE_LAYOUT`); a single `\n` with no blank line is a contract defect, markdown renders it fused onto the service line as one run-on. This session's milestones, each rendered ` `, with a status marker chosen for legibility on BOTH light and dark themes — no half-tone shading characters (`░ ▒ ▓`) anywhere, they vanish depending on theme. Status set: `✅` done · `👷` active (the step running now) · `◻️` not yet reached. Delta only; never re-list everything already settled. This is the «where are we», and it replaces a verbose run-on of finished steps.
`Vision ✅ · Scope Graph 👷 · Infra ◻️ · Portal ◻️`
The agent's compressed read of the task — its own confirmation of blind spots so the operator can catch a misread. A `### 🤔 Как я понял задачу` section near the TOP, then an italic blockquote, 2–3 sentences: the essence + the single riskiest assumption, with the assumption linked to the question that resolves it BY WORDING — there are no question numbers or IDs left to point at, so name the question itself. Never a restate of settled content.
### 🤔 Как я понял задачу > квинтэссенция — что считаю главным. > **Где могу ошибаться:** самое хрупкое допущение — это вопрос «<формулировка вопроса>».
A sub-topic dive inside a step collapses to two lines, not a five-field Return Summary:
→ ушли в `<тема>` ← `<итог одной фразой>`
When a decision is about a flow — data moving, state transitions, start / stop conditions — draw a tiny ASCII diagram; one glance beats a paragraph. This is the one place a fenced block is allowed inside an operator message (alignment matters). Keep it small.
``` [сеть] [auth] [конфиг] ──всё есть──► ОПРОС идёт ▲ │ └──── снова есть ──── ПАУЗА ◄───────┘ что-то пропало ```
Decision first, reasoning on demand. The must-read top of a message is short: where we are + my read + what to decide. Everything heavy — full option comparison, evidence, the change-list, derivations — goes BELOW a `### ↓ Детали — по желанию` header. Never dump reasoning above the questions. Facts already verified collapse to one line («сверился: …»); uncertainties that need the operator BECOME the questions — never list them twice.

ArtifactOutput.Contract:
One line per entry — no Status/Recorded fields, no multi-line block. The parenthetical carries only what applies; omit a clause entirely rather than writing it empty.
```markdown -DL-N — (почему: ; отвергнуто: ; риск: ) ```
**ID.** `-DL-` — spec acronym first, exactly like a Task-ID and like `-REQ-` (`REQUIREMENT_ENTRY_FORMAT`); `` is sequential within THIS spec only — the acronym gives global uniqueness, not the number. Replaces the old file-local `D-NNN` (unique only inside one file); conflicts (a duplicate number inside one spec) are caught mechanically, the same way as for `-REQ-`.
Superseding a prior decision appends `; supersedes: -DL-M` to the parenthetical instead of a separate field — the entry stays one line. `` is the recording date (`YYYY-MM-DD`); status (active / superseded / rejected / deferred) is implicit from prose and from whether a later entry supersedes this one — a spec has no dangling "rejected" or "deferred" entries sitting as if active, the prose says so directly (e.g. `отвергнуто в пользу X` folded into the same line that would have recorded it, never a standalone rejected entry with its own `-DL-N`).
